question: What casing and orientation rules generally apply to word messages on signs?
model_answer: Direct Answer: In general, word messages on signs must be aligned horizontally and read left to right, and must use the standard wording shown in the Manual and the "Standard Highway Signs" publication. Casing rules vary by sign type: on community wayfinding guide signs, destination lettering must use mixed-case (initial capitals with lower-case letters), while all other word messages on those signs must be in all upper-case letters. For word pavement markings, multi-line messages should read in the direction of travel with the first word nearest the road user. Standards (mandatory): - "Except as otherwise provided in this Manual, all word messages shall be aligned horizontally across a sign, reading left to right." - "Except as provided in Section 2A.04, all word messages shall use standard wording as shown in this Manual and in the 'Standard Highway Signs' publication (see Section 1A.05)." - "The lettering for destinations on community wayfinding guide signs shall be a combination of lower-case letters with initial upper-case letters (see Section 2D.04). All other word messages on community wayfinding guide signs shall be in all upper-case letters." - "Standardization of these designs does not preclude further improvement by minor modifications to the orientation of symbols (see Section 2A.09), width of borders, or layout of word messages, but all shapes and colors shall be as indicated." Guidance (recommended): - "If a pavement marking word message consists of more than one line of information, it should read in the direction of travel. The first word of the message should be nearest to the road user." - "Word messages should be as brief as practical and the lettering should be large enough to provide the necessary legibility distance." Visual evidence: [Image 1] Table 2L-3 shows CMS message examples with all upper-case lettering aligned horizontally, and its note states these examples apply to single-color CMS while multi-color, full-matrix CMS with pixel spacing of 20 mm or less should use upper- and lower-case lettering where appropriate. [Image 2] Figure 9D-5 illustrates guide signing on a shared-use path, and the accompanying text applies the same casing pattern (mixed-case destination lettering, all upper-case for other word messages) to Destination Guide signs for shared-use paths. Citations: - Section 2A.08 Standard §1 (p.45) - Section 2A.08 Standard §2 (p.45) - Section 2D.55 Standard §32 (p.271) - Section 2A.04 Standard §8 (p.40) - Section 3B.21 Guidance §2 (p.575) - Section 2D.55 Guidance §28 (p.271) - Table 2L-3 (p.517) - Figure 9D-5 (p.1082)
gold_answer: Word messages generally read horizontally from left to right. Place, street, and highway names use initial upper-case letters with lower-case letters; other legends use upper-case letters unless another MUTCD provision specifies otherwise.
